title: A novel data fusion method to leverage passively-collected mobility data in generating spatially-heterogeneous synthetic population
authors: Khoa D. Vo; Eui-Jin Kim; Prateek Bansal
abstract: Conventional methods to synthesize population use household travel survey (HTS) data. They generate many infeasible attribute values due to sequentially generating sociodemographics and spatial attributes and encounter a low spatial heterogeneity issue due to a low sampling rate of the HTS data. Passively collected mobility (PCM) data (e.g., cellular traces) provides extensive spatial coverage but poses integration challenges with HTS data due to differences in spatial resolution and attributes. This study introduces a novel cluster-based data fusion method to address these limitations and simultaneously generate synthetic populations with accurate sociodemographics and home–work locations at high spatial heterogeneity. Spatial clustering is adopted to align the spatial resolution of HTS and PCM data, facilitating effective data integration. The data fusion process is reformulated into cluster-specific low-dimensional optimization subproblems to ensure computational tractability. Analytical properties are derived to retain essential distributional characteristics from both datasets in the fused distribution. The spatial clustering process is optimized to ensure such distributional consistencies while maintaining a balance between feasibility and heterogeneity of the synthetic population. The data fusion properties are validated using HTS and LTE/5G cellular signaling data from Seoul, South Korea. Validation against census data confirms the method’s efficacy in maintaining distributional consistency while increasing spatial heterogeneity, with 97% of the generated population being unobserved in the HTS data. This research advances methods to synthesize a population by leveraging the complementary strengths of HTS and PCM data, providing a robust framework for generating spatially diverse synthetic populations essential for urban planning.
abstractZh: 传统合成人口方法使用家庭出行调查（HTS）数据。由于按顺序生成社会人口属性和空间属性，常会产生许多不可行的属性值；同时，HTS采样率较低，导致空间异质性不足。被动采集移动（PCM）数据，如蜂窝网络轨迹，具有广泛空间覆盖，但与HTS数据的空间分辨率和属性不同，整合存在挑战。本研究提出一种新的基于聚类的数据融合方法，以克服上述局限，同时生成社会人口属性和居住—工作地点准确、空间异质性较高的合成人口。通过空间聚类统一HTS与PCM数据的空间分辨率，促进有效整合。将数据融合过程重新表述为针对各聚类的低维优化子问题，以保证计算可处理性。研究推导相关解析性质，使融合分布保留两个数据集的关键分布特征；并优化空间聚类过程，确保分布一致性，同时平衡合成人口的可行性与异质性。利用韩国首尔的HTS和LTE/5G蜂窝信令数据验证数据融合性质。与普查数据对照的验证表明，该方法能够在提高空间异质性的同时维持分布一致性，其中97%的生成人口未在HTS数据中被观测到。本研究利用HTS与PCM数据的互补优势，推进人口合成方法，为生成城市规划所需的空间多样性合成人口提供稳健框架。
